note: Tests that fail on the Linux runner for reasons that do not exist on this Mac. The Mac allowlist (unit-known-red.json) does NOT transfer: it names this machine's environment, and the nightly runs ubuntu-24.04-arm. An entry here is a claim with evidence, not a mute button — check it with `node local/check-nightly-linux-parity.mjs --failures <downloaded-artifacts>`, which fails on any red that is not listed and reports a listed test that passed as prunable. An entry stores Vitest's full name, describe chain included, and pins the cause with `match`; a bare title no longer absorbs anything, and an entry with no `match` that is not `flaky: true` is a problem. The 2026-11-05 upstream move of this file (2f217b4d0dd) left its entry naming a path no report contains, so the red it exists to absorb was not being absorbed at all until #317 corrected the path, the name and the cause together.

entries.test: DaemonPtyAdapter history recovery serializes concurrent keepHistory and disconnectOnly checkpoints
entries.evidence: Failed on Linux three times: run 40485647652 (scheduled, nplez1/main @7c53c12a17) and run 40517494613 (dispatch, nplez1/main @ddc2a7827f), both with DaemonConnectionLostError: Disconnected out of disconnectOnly() at the test's own line 292, and again in run 40675428994 (scheduled 2026-10-28, nplez1/main @7b86cb08), where local/check-unit-shard-verdict.mjs absorbed it as an already-triaged red. Passed in every run since: 40695078222 (dispatch, nplez1/main @d96a57ffc6 — shard 3 green; that run failed only shard 1's cooldown assertion), 40701735011 (dispatch, nplez1/main @1776dcc575, all five shards) and 40797794635 (dispatch, nplez1/main @fdd5850d0f, all five shards), the last two also reporting it as a prunable entry. It is intermittent rather than deterministic — earlier pass: 40540799557 on branch nplez1/Fork-Opt-P2 @e2f7f28789. Passes 3/3 on this Mac too, so it is not a Mac allowlist entry either. Every file in the stack is upstream-owned with zero fork hunks: daemon-pty-event-subscriptions.ts, daemon/client.ts, daemon-client-pending-requests.ts, daemon-pty-adapter.ts and the test itself. Not fixable inside the fork without divergence, which costs more at the next sync than the red costs now.
entries.exit: Remove when upstream serialises finishDisconnectOnly against in-flight requests, or when this test passes on Linux in five consecutive scheduled nights. Two would be too weak on this history: three failures in seven observations make a chance double-pass about 1 in 3 with nothing fixed, and every pass so far is a dispatch. Seen so far, in order: failed(scheduled), failed(dispatch), passed(dispatch), failed(scheduled), passed(dispatch), passed(dispatch), passed(dispatch).

entries.test: offscreen browser page frame rate ticks unwatched pages slowly and leased pages at full rate
entries.evidence: Failed on GitHub's ubuntu-latest runner in the release dispatch run 43815938893 (nplez1/orca @6e334224aaf, shard 9/12) with `unwatched: +0` — the offscreen page painted no frame at all in the two-second sample, where the test allows up to 15 at ~5 fps. The suite launches a real Electron process through runElectronFixture and counts painted frames; a headless Linux runner has no compositor to paint into, so the number is a property of the runner rather than of the code. The same file is in UNIT_EXCLUDE on this Mac, so the local gate never runs it: it passed here only because it does not run here. Every file in the stack is upstream-owned (the test is upstream #42660 and the fixture is `testing/offscreen-page-frame-rate-electron-fixture.ts`), with no fork hunk, so it cannot be repaired inside the fork without divergence the next sync re-resolves.
entries.exit: Remove when the fixture paints frames on a headless ubuntu runner (or the test asserts a capability probe instead of a frame count), or when it passes on Linux in three consecutive dispatches.

entries.test: freeing idle offscreen browser pages frees an idle saved page and wakes it under the same id with its history
entries.evidence: Failed on GitHub's ubuntu-latest runner in the release dispatch run 43816871557 (nplez1/orca @9e7fe427014, shard 10/12): the fixture's output disagreed with the expected object while `unsavedKept` matched, i.e. the offscreen page never reached the state the assertions describe. Same fixture family and same cause as the frame-rate suite above: runElectronFixture launches a real Electron process and depends on an offscreen page actually loading and painting, which a headless runner does not provide. The file is in UNIT_EXCLUDE on this Mac, so the local gate never runs it and has no way to see the red. All files in the stack are upstream-owned with no fork hunk.
entries.exit: Remove when the fixture reaches its expected state on a headless ubuntu runner, or when it passes on Linux in three consecutive dispatches.

unhandledErrors.evidence: monaco-editor's own CancellationError raised when the editor is disposed; the stack names no repository file and no test. Observed on both machines, in runs whose only named failures were already triaged.

LOCAL-PATCHES.md records a node-runtime worker dying mid-run on this pool; it names no test, and the run it came from had every named failure already triaged. The Mac manifest carries the same headline, but only this entry sets `explainsFailure: false`: the shard verdict judges a Linux shard against its assignment, and a worker that died can lose tests inside a file the report still lists, so a crash cannot be the only explanation for a failed shard — it is tolerable only beside a known red that already explains the exit. `local/gate-unit.mjs` does not read the field.

The browser-mode dev server cannot serve Monaco's TypeScript worker from the dependency store — the URL embeds the store path, which differs per machine and per runner. No repository file appears in it and no test asserts on it.
